detail.abstract: The economics of revenge examines how vengeful motives perpetuate conflict persistence, resource misallocation, and inefficiency. This paper extends greed-grievance models by embedding emotional retaliation into rational choice theory, then applies the framework to Sudan's Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)-Rapid Support Forces (RSF) war. It uniquely integrates historical relations (colonial centralism, post-independence Arabization), racial and ethnic causes (Arab-versus-African identity as political capital), demographic and environmental pressures (desertification, population growth, resource scarcity), and bad governance (predatory rent-seeking, legal pluralism failure). A two-period game-theoretic model with spite-dependent revenge utility shows that even moderate spite (*r* = 0.3) reduces welfare by 40%, trapping belligerents in a Pareto-inferior equilibrium. Calibrated with RSF's $260 M annual gold revenue, the model predicts a 42% GDP contraction-matching empirical forecasts. Policy simulations indicate that gold sanctions (raising cost *c*) and inclusive mediation (lowering spite *r*) can shift the equilibrium toward cooperation. The paper provides 12 tables and 3 mermaid diagrams to visualize causal chains, historical timelines, and equilibrium dynamics.

title: Schumpeter Meets Pasinetti: Entrepreneurship and Income Distribution
affiliations: Florida Atlantic University and University of Brasilia

detail.title: Schumpeter Meets Pasinetti: Entrepreneurship and Income Distribution
detail.abstract: This paper explores a much-neglected issue: the relationship between entrepreneurship and income distribution. It does so by combining two major strands of economic thought: Schumpeter's theory of entrepreneurship-driven innovation (under different specifications) and the Kaldor-Pasinetti functional income distribution framework. Three models with distinct entrepreneurial activity are studied, namely, trial-and-error, entrepreneurial learning, and entrepreneurial ecosystem. We show that, while the equilibrium rate of profits is entirely given by the Cambridge equation in all formulations, a higher degree of entrepreneurship unambiguously increases output, the capital stock, and real wages. Under the assumptions of the models developed in this paper, entrepreneurship can thus be seen as a "rising tide that lifts all boats". In this context, policy reforms that promote entrepreneurship would foster innovation, productivity, and higher real wages. However, the impact of entrepreneurship on the distribution of national income between wages and profits as well as on the distribution of the total capital stock between workers and capitalists is parameterdependent and therefore ambiguous.

title: When AI Agents Spend Your Money: Card Rails, Stablecoins, and the Coming Lock-In of Agentic Commerce
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: When AI Agents Spend Your Money: Card Rails, Stablecoins, and the Coming Lock-In of Agentic Commerce
detail.abstract: Agentic commerce, in which autonomous AI software purchases goods on behalf of consumers, is emerging faster than the academic literature has documented. Two competing payment architectures have materialized. Tokenized card networks, led by Visa and Mastercard, offer reversibility and dispute resolution. Stablecoin protocols, led by Coinbase's x402, offer finality and microtransaction viability. This paper argues that these are not mere technical variants but incompatible economic and legal logics. The card model embeds consumer protection through ex post reversibility. The stablecoin model embeds efficiency through ex ante cryptographic finality. Through a synthesis of recent academic literature and industry developments, we show that neither architecture can fully incorporate the other's core logic. We further argue that payment preferences exhibit strong path dependence and switching costs, making early consumer delegation decisions prone to lock-in. The paper concludes by identifying open research questions at the intersection of payments economics, consumer protection law, and agentic system design.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Relative Adaptive Velocity (RAV) framework: a theory of organizational survivability under AIaccelerated competitive conditions in which survival probability is determined not by absolute AI capability level but by peerrelative adoption velocity. The central claim is that AI creates recursive capability compounding — through proprietary operational data generation, decision-loop compression, and continuously improving autonomous systems — such that the competitive baseline itself becomes dynamic and increasingly difficult for lagging firms to reach through conventional catchup investment. This is a structural argument, not a technology argument: the mechanism is coordination economics, and the theoretical lineage runs from Coase through Hannan and Freeman. The framework develops four primary contributions. First, it reframes survivability as a relativistic rather than absolute phenomenon, situating this claim against dynamic capabilities theory, AI maturity models, and technological discontinuity literature. Second, it introduces the Relative Adaptive Velocity construct and a proposed composite measurement methodology for estimating peer-relative adaptation position. Third, it develops an ecological governance model in which executive leadership shifts from local optimization toward systemic homeostasis management across interconnected organizational subsystems. Fourth, it proposes a systemic contribution incentive architecture designed to align compensation with organizational coherence rather than siloed productivity — with explicit development of both the logic and the genuine constraints of this model. The paper further examines the macroeconomic implications of recursive AI adoption dynamics, including market concentration through data asymmetry, labor market bifurcation, firm mortality patterns, the productivity paradox reexamined, systemic fragility in critical sectors, and institutional incoherence in public governance. The framework is presented as a theoretical model generating testable propositions rather than as an empirically validated predictive system. It is the first application paper in a research program whose coordination economics foundations are developed in the companion foundational paper, The New Coordination Economics: Organizational Adaptation When Information Physics Change. Its purpose is to provide conceptual structure for understanding the organizational, competitive, and institutional consequences of peer-relative AI adoption dynamics — and to identify the research agenda required to validate, extend, or productively challenge its central claims.

title: The Collateral Trap: Overhauling Bangladesh's CMSME Credit Architecture and Transitioning to Data-Driven Cash-Flow Lending

detail.title: The Collateral Trap: Overhauling Bangladesh's CMSME Credit Architecture and Transitioning to Data-Driven Cash-Flow Lending
detail.abstract: The Cottage, Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (CMSME) sector constitutes the structural backbone of Bangladesh's developing economy, contributing approximately 25% to the national GDP and anchoring nearly 80% of non-agricultural employment. Despite its macroeconomic criticality, the sector suffers from chronic, systemic credit starvation, evidenced by an estimated $2.8 billion financing gap. This paper argues that the persistent credit crunch is fundamentally a supply-side structural failure, driven by an obsolete banking paradigm that over-relies on immovable physical collateral rather than forward-looking cash-flow productivity. Utilizing systems thinking and the Stiglitz-Weiss credit rationing framework, this paper deconstructs the institutional dynamics, information asymmetries, and bureaucratic friction-specifically the weaponization of compliance and regulatory circulars-that systematically disenfranchise asset-light entrepreneurs. By examining successful digitized lending infrastructures in India, Vietnam, and Malaysia, this study outlines a comprehensive, four-pillar strategic roadmap encompassing unified digital identities, alternative credit underwriting, regulatory provisioning recalibration, and end-to-end workflow automation. The objective is to shift Bangladesh's financial architecture from an asset-backed legacy model to a high-velocity, data-driven credit ecosystem capable of sustaining advanced middle-income growth.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural forces driving Sudan toward regional fragmentation, arguing that the most likely long-term outcome of the current civil war is not a two-state solution (Army vs. RSF) but a cascading sequence of secessions beginning in the eastern coastal strip. Drawing on demographic transition theory, geoeconomic analysis, resource curse literature, and comparative case studies from the Ottoman Empire, Soviet Union, Yugoslavia, and contemporary Africa, the paper demonstrates that Eastern Sudan possesses the economic viability-including $1.6-2.15 billion in annual revenues from port fees, oil transit, gold exports, and agriculture-to sustain an independent state. The analysis further explores how external actors (Eritrea and the UAE) may accelerate this process, and how the subsequent disintegration of Darfur, the Nuba Mountains, and the northern Nile rump state would follow a domino pattern. In response to this fragmentation risk, the paper proposes the "Shield State" development model: a framework of selective self-sufficiency, strategic raw material export bans, knowledge sovereignty, genderinclusive industrialization, green industrial policy, and conditional foreign engagement designed to break Sudan's structural plunder economy. Drawing on successful transformations in Ethiopia, Rwanda, and Bangladesh, the paper demonstrates that structural transformation is possible even from conditions of extreme fragility. The paper concludes that Sudan's disintegration is not inevitable but requires urgent institutional reform, anti-smuggling enforcement, a political coalition of producers, and credible implementation of the Shield State model to make unity more economically beneficial than secession. Policy recommendations for Sudanese and international actors are provided.

title: Do Small Shareholders Have a Voice? Deliberation, Delegation, and Value in DAO Governance
affiliations: , University College London - Department of Computer Science, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (SUFE) - Dishui Lake Advanced Finance Institute (DAFI) and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Finance

detail.title: Do Small Shareholders Have a Voice? Deliberation, Delegation, and Value in DAO Governance
detail.abstract: We study whether small token holders have voice in the governance of decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), and whether that voice creates value. We develop a model in which the informed party is the protocol user rather than the large holder: users learn the long-run consequences of governance through protocol usage. Discussion forums aggregate users' dispersed information, and delegation concentrates their dispersed votes into a decisive bloc and lowers the cost of participation. Using account-level data on 2,830 proposals from DeFi DAOs, we find that these features raise small holders' participation and influence over outcomes. Smallholder victories are rare, but when they occur, small holders prevail by pooling their votes through delegation rather than by allying with large holders. Their victories earn positive abnormal returns, and the reaction is larger when the preceding deliberation reached more consensus. The prevailing holders hold their tokens rather than sell.

title: Three Barriers to Kantian Cooperation under Inequality
affiliations: and Higher Colleges of Technology

detail.title: Three Barriers to Kantian Cooperation under Inequality
detail.abstract: Multiplicative Kantian equilibrium, introduced by Roemer, has been proposed as a solution to inefficiency in social dilemmas, yet its emergence and stability are associated with a number of coordination and distributional difficulties. Drawing on a simple model of voluntary public good provision with two agents who differ in their initial endowments and have logarithmic preferences, this paper identifies three barriers that arise sequentially when unequal agents attempt to adopt Kantian cooperation voluntarily. The model builds on the classical setup of Bergstrom, Blume, and Varian and compares Nash equilibrium with multiplicative Kantian equilibrium under two different parametrizations: one in which the strategic variable is contributions to the public good, and another in which it is private consumption. First, we show that the transition from Nash equilibrium to contribution-space Kantian behavior is not always a Pareto improvement: under sufficiently high inequality, the poor agent may prefer the Nash outcome. This barrier can be mitigated by preliminary redistribution. Second, even when agents are willing to cooperate, the choice of a parametrization of the strategic space becomes a distributional issue: different ways of scaling actions lead to different distributive consequences and create a conflict of interest between agents. Third, if the chosen parametrization admits a continuum of Pareto-efficient outcomes, an additional coordination problem arises-agreeing on a specific point on the Pareto frontier. The paper reconstructs these barriers as a three-step coordination problem in which expectations about later stages affect agents' willingness to enter Kantian cooperation at the outset. On the basis of the results obtained, a program for further formal research is outlined. The findings contribute to understanding the conditions under which Kantian cooperation can be voluntarily adopted and sustainably maintained.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates gym and fitness facility penetration in Brazil in response to a recurring market-data gap: widely cited penetration rates do not always make clear which numerator is used, which types of facilities are included, or which assumptions convert observed units into users. To address this limitation, the paper proposes a bottom-up estimate based on active CNPJs in CNAE 9313-1/00, identification of mapped leading chains, operational classification of units outside those chains, active building-condominium records, and Monte Carlo simulation to propagate uncertainty. The gym layer uses public Federal Revenue Service data with base month 2024-09 and identifies 66,302 active CNPJs associated with fitness-conditioning activities, of which 1,651 are classified as mapped leading gym chains. Although they represent only 2.5% of active units, these chains account for 14.8% of estimated users in the reference scenario. The national estimate is probabilistic: the simulation indicates a median of 8.27%, with an 80% interval from 6.93% to 9.75%. Therefore, Brazilian penetration should be read as a plausible range conditional on assumptions, not as a single number. Because the numerator aggregates infrastructure layers, the results represent estimated recurring reach rather than a deduplicated count of unique individuals. Territorial results are also presented with uncertainty: state capitals reach 11.12% in the reference scenario, with a conservative-optimistic range from 5.94% to 18.57%, compared with 6.85% in other municipalities, with a range from 3.56% to 11.41%. The findings indicate that the Brazilian discussion should not be limited to an aggregate national percentage, but should consider operational composition, territorial differences, condominium infrastructure and methodological transparency.

detail.title: Constraints Affecting the Adoption of Low-Carbon Agricultural Technologies in Kerala

publicationDetails.detailsText: Indian Journal of Extension Education, volume 62, issue 1, 2026[10.48165/IJEE.2026.621RN07 ]

detail.abstract: The study was conducted during 2025 in the three districts of Kerala, viz., Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, and Kasaragod, to identify the most critical constraints to farmers’ adoption of low-carbon agricultural technologies (LCAT). A descriptive research design was administered for data collection, and 270 farmers were selected using random sampling technique. The Garrett ranking technique was applied to quantify the severity of ten predetermined constraints influencing adoption. The results revealed that unpredictable weather, labour shortage, and high input costs were the most severe constraints limiting adoption. Economic and market-related barriers, including the lack of marketing facilities and inputs, also restricted farmers’ willingness to adopt low-carbon agricultural technologies. Knowledge-related constraints, including limited awareness of climate change and low-carbon technologies, were ranked lower, indicating that awareness alone was inadequate to drive adoption without tackling structural and financial barriers. Spearman’s rank correlation revealed the district-wise variation in the severity of constraints, emphasising the need for location-specific extension strategies, within a broader state-level policy framework to promote Kerala’s transition towards carbonneutral agriculture.

title: Ramsey and Expected Utility Theory
affiliations: University of Siena - Department of Economics and Statistics

detail.title: Ramsey and Expected Utility Theory
detail.abstract: This paper is a contribution to the Cambridge Companion to Frank Ramsey, edited by Pedro Duarte and Cheryl Misak, CUP (forthcoming). The paper traces Ramsey’s role in the development of the subjective version of expected utility theory, which remains largely the predominant theory of economic decision-making under uncertainty to this day. The paper focuses primarily on the aspects of problem formulation suggested by Ramsey, who is unanimously regarded as the founder of the subjective approach alongside—though independently of—Bruno de Finetti. It also reconstructs the stages of its gradual acceptance beginning in the 1950s, particularly the recognition by Jacob Marschak and Leonard Savage that Ramsey’s pragmatic approach contained both the philosophical foundations and the formal structure of a theory of rationality in economics. Finally, the paper briefly considers whether the vision of strict rationality usually attributed to Ramsey should be viewed merely as a first step toward a wider analysis of the reasonableness of decisions, although Ramsey was unable to actually develop it before his untimely death, as noted by John Maynard Keynes.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we make the case for an integrated approach that combines philosophical analysis with historical research to write the recent history of economics as a history of interconnections between economics and other fields. Building on Hasok Chang's cyclical model of integrating history and philosophy of science, we argue that philosophical concepts can play an important epistemic role in historiography and outline its key features visa -vis other historiographical traditions. To demonstrate the epistemic value of such an integrated approach, we apply it to two episodes of model transfer in the history of game theory, showing how it illuminates economics' interconnections with other sciences.

title: Impact of Global Interest Rate Hikes on India's GDP Growth: Focusing on the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism (2022-2026)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Impact of Global Interest Rate Hikes on India's GDP Growth: Focusing on the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism (2022-2026)
detail.abstract: This paper tries to understand how India's economy-specifically its GDP growthwas affected by the global tightening cycle between 2022 and 2026. It focuses on the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism (MPTM), which refers to the process through which a change in the RBI's policy interest rate (the repo rate) eventually affects economic activity, credit, prices, and exchange rates. The paper examines three main transmission channels: the interest rate channel, the bank credit channel, and the exchange rate channel, alongside how India managed the Impossible Trinity. The main argument of this paper is that while India was clearly affected by global rate hikes-especially through capital outflows and Rupee depreciation-it showed a surprising degree of resilience. Strong government spending on infrastructure, a booming services sector, and the RBI's smart use of liquidity tools helped the economy maintain above-average growth throughout the period from FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electricity Market Resilience: Integrating Price Forecasting, Electric Vehicle Flexibility, and Digital Energy Infrastructures
affiliations: Beijing Normal University

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electricity Market Resilience: Integrating Price Forecasting, Electric Vehicle Flexibility, and Digital Energy Infrastructures
detail.abstract: The accelerating convergence of renewable energy deployment and electric-vehicle diffusion is reshaping electricity markets by introducing new forms of variability, demand flexibility, and price uncertainty. While these transitions support decarbonization, they also weaken the reliability of traditional price-forecasting models that were designed for relatively stable generation and consumption patterns. This study develops a technology-oriented discussion on how artificial intelligence and digital energy infrastructures can strengthen the accuracy, resilience, and adaptability of energy price forecasting under volatile market conditions. It examines the role of machine-learning forecasting models, digital twins, blockchain-supported energy trading, data-driven volatility assessment, and vehicle-to-grid mechanisms in improving market responsiveness and price stability. Rather than treating these tools as isolated innovations, the study argues for an integrated system-level framework that connects forecasting intelligence, decentralized transactions, flexible EV participation, and real-time market monitoring. The review further identifies unresolved challenges related to algorithmic transparency, model compatibility, regulatory acceptance, decision-support accountability, and performance validation across different market scenarios. By linking digitalization, artificial intelligence, and sustainability-oriented market design, this study highlights how future energy forecasting systems can move beyond prediction accuracy alone and contribute to more stable, adaptive, and low-carbon energy markets.

detail.abstract: Ethiopia was never colonized, yet its women have lost economic ground. Across pre-colonial Africa, women often owned land, controlled trade, and held authority. Historical records from Ethiopia show female landholders, judges, and market leaders. Then came modernisation. Western education, foreign legal codes, and a cash economy valued men's wage labour over women's traditional work. Even without a colonial flag, patriarchal norms quietly took root. Today, the economic cost of such gender gaps is immense. Sub-Saharan Africa loses an estimated $95 billion every year due to gender inequality, according to the UNDP (2016). In Ethiopia, fewer than eight per cent of women hold paid jobs, and over ninety per cent work in the informal economy with no protection. This paper traces the journey from pre-colonial economic partnership to modern exclusion, quantifies the cost, and offers five affordable, Africa-led solutions. It argues that restoring women's economic power is not a favour. It is the fastest path to shared prosperity.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based co-optimization of sizing and operation of energy storage in port energy-logistics system considering second-life battery
affiliations: Wuhan University of Technology, Ningbo University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Zhejiang University, Charleston Southern University, Aalto University and Aalborg University

detail.title: Deep reinforcement learning-based co-optimization of sizing and operation of energy storage in port energy-logistics system considering second-life battery
detail.abstract: Port Integrated Multi-Energy System (PIMES) must simultaneously decarbonize high-intensity logistics operations and absorb the surge of retired electric-vehicle batteries, yet existing studies seldom consider second-life-batteries (SLBs) and real-time energy-logistics dispatch. This study proposes a bilevel co-optimization framework coupling gradient-descent capacity sizing with a Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MAML-DDPG) dispatcher to adaptively coordinate degradation-aware planning and real-time energy-logistics scheduling. The objective function jointly minimizes replacement, operation, electricity-purchase, load-shedding, and logistics costs. Validated over a 20-year horizon synthesized by cyclically extending three years (2020–2022) of measured operational data from the Ningbo-Zhoushan Port, the framework reduces the lifecycle cost from 1044.3 to 859.2 million CNY, a 17.7% saving, with electricity-purchase cost down 14.5%, load-shedding cost halved, and logistics cost cut by 18.9%. The optimal sizing converges to 5250 kWh Energy Storage System (ESS) and 990 kWh Power Energy Storage Systems (PESS) in only forty gradient steps. Under an extreme islanding event, daily resilience loss is suppressed by 69.9%. The framework offers a quantitative decision-support tool for sustainable port electrification.

title: Multi-agent cooperative centralized management of industrial heat-electrical integrated energy system based on load prediction, incipient fault warning and fault recovery decision
affiliations: North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, North China Electric Power University and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: Multi-agent cooperative centralized management of industrial heat-electrical integrated energy system based on load prediction, incipient fault warning and fault recovery decision
detail.abstract: Centralized management is critical for the efficient and safe operation of an integrated energy system. In practice, fragmented management solutions focus on a single aspect of operations, such as load forecasting or fault detection, while overlooking the collaborative management of the entire integrated energy system under real-world operating conditions. To address it, a multi-agent centralized management method based on load prediction, incipient fault warning, and fault recovery decision is proposed for an industrial heat-electrical integrated energy system (IHE-IES), in which two types of agents are designed in this framework: one is a lightweight task-specific (LTS-based) discriminative agent, the other is a large language model-based (LLM-based) generative agent. Specifically, an LTS-based discriminative agent handles real-time specific load prediction and incipient fault warning tasks that require high efficiency and low latency but involve relatively regular patterns well within the capacity of compact models. In contrast, fault recovery decision-making demands reasoning over specialized domain expert knowledge across different industrial subsystems in IHE-IES and the generation of structured, professional fault logs. Based on the LTS-based discriminative agent’s prediction and detection results, an LLM-based generative agent, embedded with an IHE-IES fault knowledge graph retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach, is developed to provide professional, structured, and context-aware fault recovery decisions. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed management method achieves superior performance. For load prediction, the accuracy improves by an average of 32.51% and 19.36% compared to state-of-the-art methods on short- and long-term prediction. For the incipient fault warning, the fault detection rate increases by an average of 8.93%. For fault recovery decision-making, the proposed agent demonstrates better fault recovery generation capability than LLMs with equivalent parameter counts. As one of the first few studies to cooperate multiple agents in IHE-IES operation management, it provides a novel, effective centralized operation management scheme for IHE-IES.

title: Multiple Motivational Routes to Creativity: How Empowerment and Delegation Shape Incremental and Radical Creativity Through Dualistic Passion and Vision Awareness
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Multiple Motivational Routes to Creativity: How Empowerment and Delegation Shape Incremental and Radical Creativity Through Dualistic Passion and Vision Awareness
detail.abstract: This study examines how distinct leadership practices, employee empowerment and task delegation, shape creativity through differentiated pathways of work passion, and how organizational vision awareness strengthens these motivational processes. Drawing on structural empowerment theory, psychological empowerment theory, and self-determination theory, we develop a moderated mediation framework that positions harmonious and obsessive passion as central mechanisms linking leadership practices to incremental and radical creativity. Using survey data from 531 employees across two ministries in Namibia’s public sector, analyzed with confirmatory factor analysis and bootstrapped regression models, we find that empowerment predicts harmonious passion, which in turn fosters both incremental and radical creativity, while delegation predicts obsessive passion, which is more strongly associated with incremental creativity. Organizational vision awareness amplifies these leadership-to-passion pathways, underscoring the importance of shared vision in bureaucratic contexts. By distinguishing empowerment from delegation and clarifying their passion-based mechanisms, this study advances leadership theory by showing that creativity in public organizations emerges through multiple motivational routes that depend on vision alignment. These findings extend passion and leadership research into an underexplored African public-sector setting, offering theoretical and practical insights for leaders seeking to stimulate innovation in hierarchical environments.Keywords: Employee empowerment, organizational vision awareness, self-efficacy, work passion, radical creativity.

title: Dynamic Rescheduling in Modular Transit Systems under Real-Time Operations: A Heterogeneous CPU–GPU Approach
affiliations: Southeast University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Southeast University and Southeast University

detail.title: Dynamic Rescheduling in Modular Transit Systems under Real-Time Operations: A Heterogeneous CPU–GPU Approach
detail.abstract: Autonomous modular vehicles (AMVs) enable flexible capacity reconfiguration through pod coupling and decoupling, but their operational flexibility complicates real-time scheduling when stochastic feeder demand must be integrated into scheduled service. This paper studies a real-time dynamic rescheduling problem that preserves scheduled service integrity while exploiting temporal slack in baseline pod trip chains, where baseline operations are constructed through scheduled pod trip generation and chaining and updated online through a rolling-horizon framework. The resulting large-scale, strongly NP-hard problem is solved using a heterogeneous CPU–GPU adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) that combines CPU-based adaptive control with GPU-parallelized destroy-and-repair and conflict resolution, achieving scalable real-time performance under high-demand conditions with substantial computational gains over CPU baselines.

title: Optimal Planning of Modular Non-Stop Trains under Spatially Heterogeneous Demand
affiliations: New York University Abu Dhabi, affiliation not provided to SSRN, New York University Abu Dhabi and New York University (NYU) - New York University, Abu Dhabi

detail.title: Optimal Planning of Modular Non-Stop Trains under Spatially Heterogeneous Demand
detail.abstract: The stop-and-go operation of passenger rail systems leads to longer travel times and higher energy consumption, increasing costs for both users and operators. To address this issue, this study examines a newly proposed non-stop train (NST) concept, in which intermediate-station service is provided through station-level coupling and decoupling of modular units while the cruising module maintains line speed. We first develop analytical models for both conventional all-stop train (AST) and NST operations, characterizing cycle time, passenger travel time, and energy consumption, which together form the basis of a generalized-cost function. The generalized cost jointly captures operator costs, including train and unit operating costs as well as energy cost and user costs, including passenger waiting and in-vehicle travel time costs. Building on this operating-cost and service model, we develop an integrated planning optimization framework that determines the number of trains, the number of units per train, and, for NSTs, station-level unit allocation decisions. Structural monotonicity results reduce the original mixed-integer planning problem to an exact one-dimensional search over the number of trains, enabling efficient identification of the global optimum. We apply the framework to the KTX Gyeongbu corridor in South Korea under spatially heterogeneous real-world demand. Results show that the optimized NST configuration yields a 16.7% lower minimum hourly generalized cost than the AST benchmark. Sensitivity analyses confirm that this advantage remains robust across a wide range of demand and parameter settings, while highlighting a trade-off between operator and user costs. A budget-constrained analysis further supports the cost advantage of NSTs under equal operator expenditure limits.

title: Probe-Conditioned Memory for Actuator-Deadband-Aware Koopman MPC in Industrial Sealing

detail.title: Probe-Conditioned Memory for Actuator-Deadband-Aware Koopman MPC in Industrial Sealing
detail.abstract: In industrial sealing and dispensing, a narrow bead recipe can keep its calibrated static pressure correct while small corrective moves are absorbed by actuator deadband; delivered pressure changes only after a direction- and history-dependent threshold is crossed. Commissioning here denotes the target setup and retuning interval after such a recipe change. A physical gluing and dispensing cell supplies pressure-to-width calibration, a fixed 16-action probe, signal-interface limits, residual scales, and actuator bounds. The resulting data define an anonymized digital-twin benchmark for paired multi-controller comparison, and the same signal path validates AK-MPC on the real system through six closed-loop 1-mm transfer scenarios. The actuator-deadband-aware Koopman model predictive controller (AK-MPC) uses finite-candidate receding-horizon Koopman MPC initialized from probe-conditioned memory (PCM), linking the pressure setpoint to probe-inferred actuator behavior, a predictor, a controller prior, and a fallback filter. During commissioning, the 16-action probe selects a nearby historical case, fits the current pressure-width relation, updates a small local dynamic correction, and supplies a pressure policy selected from feasible candidates. detail.title: Mitigating Price Spikes in Electricity Markets with Reserve Power Plants: Case Study on Germany Within the European Market
detail.abstract: Several European countries hold a substantial share of conventional generation capacity deliberately outside the electricity market as strategic reserve. These reserve power plants are often older units and only activated under exceptional conditions to ensure resource adequacy during severe scarcity situations. Recent policy discussions, motivated by concerns about frequent price spikes and their economic implications, consider allowing a temporary participation of reserve power plants in the electricity spot market. This paper analyzes the effects of such a policy within Germany on market outcomes and investment decisions in generation capacity, battery storage, and electrolysis in the European electricity market. To this end, we employ an electricity market model for the European electricity system in 2030 that endogenously determines investments, decommissioning, generation, storage operation, and hydrogen production. Reserve power plants are allowed to participate in the spot market whenever a predefined strike price is reached or exceeded. The analyzed scenarios are exogenously specified and vary with respect to the strike price and the volume of reserve capacity available for market participation. All results are evaluated in relation to a reference scenario without reserve power plant utilization. We find that allowing reserve power plants to enter the spot market can substantially reduce peak prices during scarcity periods. However, these short-term price reductions weaken scarcity signals and thereby reduce investment incentives, leading to a lower capacity expansion. As a result, prices increase in non-scarcity periods. In addition, the policy induces spillover effects in neighboring countries.

title: A Hierarchical Multi-Stage Framework for Remaining Useful Life Prediction in Automatic Sawing Machines

detail.title: A Hierarchical Multi-Stage Framework for Remaining Useful Life Prediction in Automatic Sawing Machines
detail.abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) has become a key component of modern industrial systems, enabling data-driven maintenance strategies that improve reliability, reduce downtime, and optimize operational costs. Among PdM tasks, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation plays a central role by forecasting the time before a component reaches the end of its operational life, thereby supporting proactive maintenance planning and informed decision-making. However, accurate RUL estimation remains challenging due to complex degradation dynamics, varying operating conditions, and limited failure data. This paper presents an industrial RUL estimation platform developed for MEP Saws to monitor the health of band saw blades and support human-centered predictive maintenance. The proposed solution integrates a scalable big-data architecture for industrial data acquisition, storage, and processing with a machine-learning-based prognostic service. At the core of the platform is a two-phase prognostic ML system that continuously assesses blade health through sensor-derived time-series features. The first phase identifies early degradation states, while the second phase predicts imminent failure through a staged warning mechanism designed to balance timely detection and false-alarm mitigation. Presenting therefore an end-to-end, RUL-based prognostic system that combines scalable industrial data management, machine learning, and human-centered decision support, providing actionable insights for more effective maintenance strategies in real-world manufacturing environments.

detail.title: Integrating ethical risks into Performance Management in Industry 4.0: the concept of Ethical Performance Indicator
detail.abstract: The widespread adoption of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) technologies is improving performance and reshaping Performance Management (PM) by increasing traceability and reinforcing decision-making through real-time Performance Indicators (PIs) supporting operational production. However, these technologies may also pose ethical risks related to excessive surveillance, work intensification, or reduced operator autonomy, which can strengthen short-term performance but undermine the long-term performance sought to be sustained. Despite their growing recognition, traditional PM systems are often disconnected from ethical governance, which is typically managed by legal departments via compliance procedures or strategic guidelines. As a result, current responses remain global or strategic and are insufficiently integrated into production activities and operational PM. To bridge this gap, the paper introduces the Ethical Performance Indicator (E-PI), a PI that expresses performance obtained under ethical conditions. The E-PI is the ethical transformation of a conventional PI, through its constitutive elements (objective, measurement, and action variable). Based on this principle, a three-step method is proposed to mitigate ethical risks by considering E-PIs. The proposed approach is illustrated on a bearing manufacturer undergoing digitalization, where the Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), under production-acceleration pressure, is transformed into an Ethical OEE (E-OEE) that integrates ethical production losses into its measurement and reinterprets its objective. The case shows that E-OEE makes production pressure visible by reclassifying hidden ethical losses in classical OEE. The research provides an approach for embedding ethical risk mitigation into operational PIs, while highlighting the need for structured ethical data, internal capabilities, and further validation across sectors.

detail.title: Interactive Human-AI Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: a Sliding Work Sharing Framework with Digital Twin Simulation
detail.abstract: With the growing need for flexible and adaptive production systems, this paper presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven framework for manufacturing scheduling that supports human operators in advanced decision-making. The framework enables a context-sensitive allocation of decision authority between human and AI actors through a sliding work sharing paradigm while ensuring transparent human oversight.The framework integrates an Optimized Decision-Maker, which automatically generates feasible schedules based on activities, resources, and constraints, with a Digital Twin that simulates schedule execution and computes relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). These KPIs are analyzed by a Sliding Work Sharing (SWS) component that leverages fuzzy-rule-based reasoning to determine the appropriate level of human involvement in validating or refining the generated decision.Through a Graphical User Interface, human users can monitor KPIs and SWS recommendations, perform what-if analyses, and introduce additional constraints. This interactive process operates in real time, enabling schedules to adapt to changing operational conditions.Developed within the EU-funded Ai4Work project, the framework supports line managers in scheduling replenishment activities for the E-CO Flex box-forming machine by I.M.A. S.p.A.. In the presented case study, plan robustness, reflecting the line's ability to sustain throughput, and worker well-being are considered the primary KPIs, balancing production efficiency with human-centered objectives.Obtained results demonstrate effective integration of human input and positive user acceptance, highlighting the framework's potential to foster productive human–AI collaboration in smart manufacturing.

title: When Good Returns Calm Volatility: Revisiting the Monthly Leverage Effect
affiliations: University of Agder - School of Business and Law

detail.title: When Good Returns Calm Volatility: Revisiting the Monthly Leverage Effect
detail.abstract: This paper reexamines the relation between past returns and future volatility at the monthly frequency. The analysis is motivated by evidence that conventional downside-only specifications of the leverage effect provide weak support in monthly data. We argue that this does not mean that the leverage effect disappears. Rather, the leverage effect changes form when returns are measured over monthly horizons. Using data on 21 U.S. equity portfolios, we show that the relevant return-based predictor is not a purely downside-only term, but the signed monthly return itself, after controlling for volatility persistence and the magnitude of return innovations. Negative monthly returns predict higher future volatility, while positive monthly returns predict lower future volatility. The signedreturn specification typically outperforms both a baseline volatility model and a downside-only specification in-sample and in recursive out-of-sample forecasts. These results suggest that monthly volatility predictability is best understood as a signed-return form of the leverage effect: negative returns signal high-volatility states, whereas positive returns signal calmer, lower-volatility states.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces and theorizes the V.P.C. Triad. A practical leadership framework grounded in three operational behaviors: being Visible, Present, and Communicative within organizational environments. Although the V.P.C. Triad is not yet formally established in academic literature as a named model, its conceptual foundations are strongly supported by established research in Management by Walking Around (MBWA), leadership walkarounds, relational leadership theory, psychological safety, leader-member exchange theory, and organizational communication. This paper argues that leadership effectiveness is not solely strategic or positional — it is operational, relational, and continuously practiced. The framework is proposed with particular applicability to healthcare administration, hospital operations, clinical leadership, emergency management, and complex service environments. Evidence from peer-reviewed literature supports each pillar of the framework, and the paper outlines the interdependent structure of the triad alongside the organizational outcomes associated with consistent application. The V.P.C. Triad offers practitioners a simple, memorable, and evidence-supported model for improving frontline leadership effectiveness.

detail.abstract: The AFT EU Market Readiness Instrument is a decision grade diagnostic framework for small and medium sized enterprises considering entry into the European Union single market. It assesses whether a firm is ready to move towards EU market entry, where its main blockers sit, and what evidence must be produced before resources are committed. detail.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in corporate decision-making, shifting from operational automation toward strategic participation. Yet managerial adoption of AI-generated insights remains uneven, shaped by algorithmic trust, algorithmic aversion, and organisational readiness for human-AI collaboration. Objective: This systematic literature review synthesises peer-reviewed research on human-AI collaboration in strategic and managerial decision-making, with emphasis on algorithmic trust, algorithmic aversion, and Centaur (human-AI partnership) models within digital management. Method: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched Scopus (Search 1 complete; Web of Science deferred) using structured Boolean queries and backward snowballing. Thematic synthesis (Thomas & Harden, 2008) integrates findings into the Centaur Strategic Decision Framework (CSDF). Results: From 45 Scopus records, 28 studies passed full-text screening; eight seminal references and eight backward-snowball studies supplemented the corpus (36 studies synthesised). Thematic synthesis (Thomas & Harden, 2008) identified seven themes: (1) algorithmic trust antecedents (n = 31; 86%), (2) algorithmic aversion mechanisms (n = 12; 33%), (3) trust calibration and appropriate reliance (n = 27; 75%), (4) explainable AI in management (n = 7; 19%), (5) Centaur/hybrid intelligence design (n = 31; 86%), (6) strategic versus operational differences (n = 15; 42%), and (7) governance and accountability (n = 8; 22%). The Centaur Strategic Decision Framework (CSDF) integrates these themes. Conclusions: The literature confirms that human-AI collaboration at the executive level is under-researched relative to operational contexts. Future empirical work should examine trust calibration in high-stakes strategic settings using mixed-methods designs. Implications are outlined for digital management practice and doctoral research.

title: A Real-time Power Consumption Anomaly Detection Method for Airport Terminal Baggage Handling Systems Based on the Principle of Information Entropy

detail.title: A Real-time Power Consumption Anomaly Detection Method for Airport Terminal Baggage Handling Systems Based on the Principle of Information Entropy
detail.abstract: As the ”aorta” of modern industrial and logistics networks, material handling systems are widely used in logistics, express delivery, aviation and other industries. As a typical motor load, their power consumption accounts for a non-negligible proportion of total energy use. Abnormalities caused by equipment failures, operational deviations or management oversights can lead to energy waste in the baggage handling system (BHS). Power consumption anomaly detection for such systems is a critical support for identifying hidden resource waste and achieving energy planning objectives. However, due to the coupling effects of multiple factors, the hourly energy consumption of BHS presents obvious non-linear fluctuations, which brings great challenges to the rapid detection and accurate diagnosis of abnormal energy consumption. To address this problem, based on the BHS operation data from January 2023 to May 2026 provided by the AMES system of a large airport terminal in China, this study develops a real-time power consumption anomaly detection method based on information entropy theory and hybrid data mining technologies. The Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) and K-means clustering algorithm are adopted to screen and extract key characteristic parameters affecting power consumption (daily passenger volume, holidays) and conduct clustering analysis, which serves as the reference for constructing the training dataset of daily information entropy calculation (January 2023 to December 2025). Combined with the K-means clustering algorithm, the demarcation point between normal and abnormal daily information entropy is determined. The range of daily hourly power consumption datasets corresponding to normal daily information entropy is regarded as the normal hourly power consumption threshold, which is used as the basis for detecting outliers in hourly power consumption data. The BHS operation data from January to May 2026 is used as the test dataset. The verification results show that the proposed daily hourly power consumption anomaly detection method, dynamically generated from historical data without subjective human intervention, has higher detection accuracy and better robustness than other common methods. The research method can provide a feasible technical path and methodological support for power consumption anomaly detection of BHS in similar airports and offer scientific reference for management departments to realize precise energy consumption control.

detail.abstract: Climate-related financial risk poses significant challenges for public companies and their investors. Yet whether issuers must disclose physical risks, transition risks, regulatory exposure, emissions-related liabilities, and stranded-asset risks is too often framed as climate policy or environmental regulation. This Article argues that it is neither. It is a question about information—and one the existing federal securities-disclosure framework is already equipped to answer. Environmental, energy, land-use, and climate-regulatory regimes generate information about climate-related exposure, including emissions, compliance costs, permitting constraints, adaptation obligations, transition costs, and asset vulnerability. Securities regulation, through the disclosure framework established by the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and the SEC’s implementing regulations, determines when that information must be provided to investors. And the First Amendment permits compelled disclosure of factual commercial information. Together, these doctrines already authorize disclosure of climaterelated financial risk when that information would matter to a reasonable investor. The shortfall is not statutory power, but implementation and enforcement. Climate-risk disclosure is not environmental regulation masquerading as securities law. It is an application of the federal securities-disclosure regime’s core premise: investors need accurate, complete, and equally available data to price risk.

detail.title: Tariffs and Strategic Upstream Sourcing
detail.abstract: We examine an upstream import shifting strategy where firms, in response to tariff increases, import upstream components and complete final assembly domestically, while keeping the rest of the value chain abroad. This approach mitigates tariff costs while preserving future flexibility. Using transaction-level shipment data and exploiting product-level tariff shocks from 2011 to 2019, we document that tariff hikes lead firms to expand imports toward more upstream inputs. The response is stronger among firms with limited cost pass-through, a shorter expected tariff horizon, lower supply-chain coordination costs, and greater tax sophistication. Upstream import shifting raises hiring for assembly work but leaves overall employment and firm scope unchanged. Our findings identify an underexplored adjustment margin bridging short-term cost management and long-term restructuring, and they reveal uneven impacts of tariff policies across firms with varying logistical and legal sophistication.

detail.abstract: Major infrastructure programmes underperform with striking consistency: across a database of more than 16,000 projects, fewer than one in a hundred deliver on time, on budget and with the benefits promised (Flyvbjerg, 2014; Flyvbjerg & Gardner, 2023). This paper argues that the dominant explanation is not delivery competence but formation: the conditions for consistent delivery are rarely put in place deliberately across the portfolio, programme and project before, or alongside, the work. It introduces the BDC Method™, a single, evidence-based standard that names the capabilities a portfolio, programme and project must hold — organised as 52 themes in four groups (Core, Level, Domain, Formation) — and renders each one measurable. The Method distinguishes itself from maturity models by asking not how mature an organisation's processes are, but whether the required capabilities are in fact in place and operating, judged on evidence. It defines three modes of application — Formation, Assessment and Remediation — and is put to work through a weighted, multi-level assessment instrument that produces a single capability score and a Red/Amber/Green profile. The approach extends the established UK practice of sponsor/client capability assessment at project initiation (HM Treasury & IPA, 2014) from a one-off review into a continuously owned, in-house standard. detail.abstract: Intelligent agent simulation has historically been constrained by a fundamental coupling: the simulation must run at the speed of the agent's decision-making process. When the decision-making agent is a large language model (LLM), this constraint becomes severeinference latency of several seconds per decision makes real-time simulation infeasible, forcing a tradeoff between agent intelligence and simulation throughput. We present inference-subordinate simulation, an architectural pattern that eliminates this constraint by inverting the relationship between simulation and inference. Rather than the simulation running continuously and the agent reacting in real time, the simulation engine advances only when the agent issues a decision. Each decision is logged with full state and timing metadata. Playback reads the decision log and reproduces identical behavior at any speed, without re-running inference. We implement this architecture using Godot 4 as the simulation engine, a Python HTTP server as the inference layer, and Claude (claude-opus-4-5) as the vision-language agent. The agent observes the 3D environment through a bird's eye camera, reasons about spatial relationships, and issues structured tool calls that advance world state. Across 26 empirical runs comprising 222 decisions, the agent achieved a 100% goal success rate with a mean inference time of 4.53 seconds per decision (σ = 1.12s) and a mean good move rate of 90.5%. Across 26 runs, the mean total inference time was 38.66 seconds per run. The same decision sequences replay in under one second at 10× speed-a demonstration that playback time is fully decoupled from inference time and adjustable as a free parameter. The representative run used to illustrate this comparison was selected to match the dataset mean, not to maximize the speedup figure. The architecture is model-agnostic at the inference layer: any vision-language model can be substituted without modifying the simulation engine or replay system. Navigation quality is model-dependent; we document the failure of a 7B local model and the successful substitution of a capable API model, treating this as an honest characterization of current model capabilities rather than an architectural limitation. We discuss applications in cinematic production, video game NPC pre-computation, reinforcement learning training data generation, and social science modeling where the real-time constraint is absent and the decoupled architecture offers substantial practical advantages.

title: Founder Factories: The Origins of High-Growth Startups

detail.title: Founder Factories: The Origins of High-Growth Startups
detail.abstract: This paper asks whether some employers influence the kinds of startups their employees later build. Using global career-history data matched to startup outcomes, we identify founders' previous employers and build an alumni startup-scale score for each employer. The score captures how often a firm's former employees go on to found startups that become unusually large, after accounting for employer size; it also predicts international reach and acquisition activity. We then study employees whose firms were acquired, which exposed them to new employers with different alumni startup-scale scores. Founders exposed to higher-score acquirers seem more ambitious in terms of scalability of their businesses at launch according to early business descriptions. We show this using archived startup websites from the founding period. These founders' startups later employ more people, operate in more countries, and more often make acquisitions. The patterns are stronger for employees who are integrated into the acquiring firm, and they are not explained by founders simply entering the acquirer's industry, hiring from the acquirer, or receiving financing from it.

title: Lift-Sample-Repair for BOM-Structured Production Planning with Agent-Assisted Policy Search

detail.title: Lift-Sample-Repair for BOM-Structured Production Planning with Agent-Assisted Policy Search
detail.abstract: We study integrated production planning and aggregate scheduling for large-scale make-to-order manufacturing. Each order carries bill-of-materials (BOM) requirements and routing operations, while orders compete for shared work-center capacity over time. Time-indexed mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations model this setting directly, but become difficult to solve at industrial scale. We propose Lift-Sample-Repair (LSR), an LP-guided rounding method that converts a fractional LP solution into a reduced set of precedence-feasible whole-order timing patterns, samples one pattern per order, and repairs sharedcapacity violations. We prove that this lift recovers a whole-order support whose size is linear in each order's operation-period grid and that the expected loss relative to the LP benchmark is sublinear under capacity granularity, with an O(√ N) bound when individual orders are small relative to capacity. These results provide theoretical support for LSR's computational efficiency and solution quality. Empirically, base LSR reaches 94%-98% of the LP benchmark at the three largest tested scales, where the original time-indexed MILP certifies only 22 of 108 attempts within a two-hour budget. A loss decomposition shows that much of the residual gap remains after pattern construction, in pattern selection and repair. This motivates Agent-LSR, which automates policy search within the modular LSR interface. An LLM coding agent searches implementable rules for sampling, repair, refill, and multi-pass selection, while the recovered pattern set, model, LP relaxation, and feasibility guard remain fixed. On challenging structured instances, it reduces the average LP-relative gap from about 24% to about 6%. In an industrial PCB case study, LSR improves LP-relative performance relative to representative planning baselines, attaining mean LP-relative gaps below 1% on a fine-grained mass-production plant and 11.4% on a coarser custom plant under Agent-LSR. Beyond constructing feasible planning schedules, the same interface turns LP capacity shadow prices into managerial diagnostics for order triage, bottleneck-capacity planning, and decentralized work-center coordination.

title: Occupational Psychological Profiles of Heavy-Haul Railway Drivers: A Latent Profile Analysis Based on Job Stressors, Job Satisfaction, Resilience, and Burnout
